events.title: Supreme Court stays mandate in Jose Duran v. United States
events.summary: The Supreme Court, through Associate Justice Sonia Sotomayor, issued an order recalling and staying the mandate of the United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit in the case of Jose Duran, individually and as representative of a class of judgment creditors of the estate of Ferdinand E. Marcos, against the United States and others. The stay is pending further order from the Court, and a response to the application is required by November 12, 2025.
events.why_relevant: The stay affects the enforcement of a lower court's decision, impacting the legal proceedings related to the judgment creditors of the Marcos estate.

events.title: Administrative Stay Granted in SNAP Funding Case
events.summary: The Supreme Court, through Associate Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson, issued an administrative stay on the orders of the United States District Court for the District of Rhode Island. These orders required the Secretary of Agriculture and others to fund and distribute Supplemental Nutritional Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits for November by the end of November 7, 2025. The stay is in place pending the First Circuit Court of Appeals' decision on a motion for a stay pending appeal. The administrative stay will terminate 48 hours after the First Circuit's decision on the pending motion.
events.why_relevant: This order temporarily halts the enforcement of a lower court's decision, affecting the distribution of SNAP benefits and highlighting the judicial process in resolving disputes over federal program funding.
